title: Repurchase smoothing and runway scenarios for reserved GPU pools
content:
Purpose
This working note documents a spreadsheet-backed approach and recommendations for 'repurchase smoothing' — a tactical pricing and commit-management pattern to reduce churn and stranded capacity risk when customers have variable usage and multi-quarter commit renewals. Goal is to produce a calculator that sales and finance can use in negotiation and PM/Eng can use to simulate utilization and margin impact.

Background and problem statement
- We sell Reserved GPU Pools (RGP) with committed monthly/quarterly GPU-hours and optional repurchase/rollover clauses.
- Large customers often face seasonal/usage volatility, causing a mismatch between committed capacity and actual consumption, leading to either: (a) customer churn at renewal, or (b) stranded idle capacity for Redwood.
- Current deals are often binary (renew full commit or not) or include one-time credits. We need a smoother, predictable cadence to: preserve revenue, reduce stranded idle hours, and keep utilization high without too much discounting.

High-level proposal
- Introduce a "repurchase smoothing" plan: customers can opt into a tapering repurchase schedule and flexible rollover pool with price tiers.
- Mechanism: at renewal, customer selects a target commit for next N months. System proposes a taper curve (e.g., 100% -> 85% -> 70% -> hold) with an associated blended effective rate and optional on-demand uplift band.
- Financial aim: preserve at least X% of committed revenue vs. full churn while increasing effective utilization and enabling backfill for freed capacity.

Spreadsheet model structure (tab-by-tab)
1) assumptions.tab (input sheet)
   - columns (each as separate named input cell): base_gpu_hour_cost (USD/hr), list_price_hour (USD/hr), avg_utilization_pct, churn_risk_no_smoothing_pct, smoothing_discount_pct, repurchase_window_months, expected_monthly_usage_profile (comma-separated series), backfill_effectiveness_pct, reserved_gpu_count, expected_gpu_hours_per_month_per_gpu
   - example values: base_gpu_hour_cost=0.35, list_price_hour=2.10, avg_utilization_pct=0.68, churn_risk_no_smoothing_pct=0.30, smoothing_discount_pct=0.12, repurchase_window_months=6, backfill_effectiveness_pct=0.45

2) schedule.tab (repurchase curve builder)
   - columns: month_index, proposed_commit_pct_of_prior, absolute_committed_hours, expected_actual_hours (from usage_profile), idle_hours = committed - actual, backfill_recovered_hours = idle_hours * backfill_effectiveness_pct, net_idle_hours = idle_hours - backfill_recovered_hours
   - formulas: absolute_committed_hours = prior_committed_hours * proposed_commit_pct_of_prior; prior_committed_hours seeded with current_commit_hours.

3) pricing.tab (blended rate and margin)
   - columns: month_index, committed_hours, effective_discount, billed_revenue = committed_hours * list_price_hour * (1 - effective_discount), cost = committed_hours * base_gpu_hour_cost, gross_margin = billed_revenue - cost, margin_pct = gross_margin / billed_revenue
   - special rows for: repurchase credit applied, on-demand uplift revenue (consumption beyond commit billed at list or premium), and net revenue after backfill credits

4) scenarios.tab (matrix)
   - Each column is a scenario. Rows contain key metrics aggregated over the repurchase_window_months: total_committed_hours, total_billed_revenue, total_cost, net_idle_hours, utilization_rate (actual_hours / committed_hours), revenue_retention_vs_full_renewal, break-even_price_adjustment.

Suggested scenario seeds (examples)
- Conservative: smoothing_discount=6%, backfill_effectiveness=20%, churn_risk_no_smoothing=35%
- Market-friendly: smoothing_discount=12%, backfill_effectiveness=45%, churn_risk_no_smoothing=28%
- Aggressive retention: smoothing_discount=18%, backfill_effectiveness=60%, churn_risk_no_smoothing=20%
- Edge-case high seasonality: usage_profile with spikes and troughs, backfill_effectiveness low (10%)

Key formulas and heuristics to implement in-sheet
- Effective_discount = base_smoothing_discount + (1 - backfill_effectiveness) * scale_factor (so if backfill is weak, discount increases slightly)
- Backfill_value_per_hour = list_price_hour * backfill_recovered_hours * backfill_capture_rate (reflects that backfilled usage might come at discount)
- Revenue_retention_vs_full_renewal = (billed_revenue_with_smoothing) / (billed_revenue_if_full_renewal)
- Break-even_adjustment: compute minimal discount required to keep customer (model churn probability as logistic function of delta_commit_vs_usage)

Operational recommendations (how to use with Sales/Finance)
- Provide a "one-click" scenario generator in the spreadsheet for Sales: inputs = current_commit, target_min_commit_pct, months_to_smooth, expected_usage_curve, desired_revenue_floor.
- Output: recommended month-by-month commit, blended rate offer, expected net revenue delta vs full renewal, suggested clause language (see draft below), and a short negotiation playbook.

Draft negotiation language (short, for AE use)
- "We can offer a 6-12% blended smoothing credit delivered over a 6-month taper. This preserves predictability for you and gives us runway to reassign capacity if your usage drops. If your consumption exceeds the rolling commit, excess usage will bill at our on-demand rate. We can agree a 2-month lookback cadence to adjust the taper if your usage materially diverges."

SLA trade-offs and policy guidance
- If a customer chooses smoothing, default SLA remains but with a lower guaranteed reserved slab for the first N months (e.g., reserve guarantee = proposed_commit_pct_of_prior * 90% for months 1-2). This avoids overcommit guaranteeing while giving the customer practical carry.
- Alternative: keep SLA unchanged but tie smoothing discount to faster remediation windows or a small platform fee to keep minimum revenue.

Sales playbook quick checks
- Run scenario: if revenue_retention_vs_full_renewal >= 0.75 and utilization_rate rises by >= 8 points, smoothing is considered acceptable.
- Avoid smoothing if backfill_effectiveness < 15% and churn_risk_no_smoothing < 10% (customer likely stable).

Open questions and follow-ups
- Exact legal wording and whether smoothing counts as a modification to committed terms (legal & finance input required).
- How to instrument telemetry to track committed vs actual on an hourly cadence and feed back to billing SAAS (billing infra ticket).
- Integrate an automatic reprice/notice email if usage deviates > 25% vs expected for two consecutive months.

Implementation checklist (engineering + product)
- [ ] Build a small calculator UI for AE console that mirrors spreadsheet outputs (frontend + API)
- [ ] Add billing flags and agreement fields (repurchase_smoothing: true, smoothing_schedule_id) in billing DB schema
- [ ] Instrument per-customer commit vs actual dashboard in Redwood Console (alerting threshold: net_idle > X hours)
- [ ] Create a small backfill marketplace internal workflow (pool for temporarily freed hours) and SLAs for reclaiming capacity

Next steps (owners)
- Product (Priya): validate model with 3 top pilot customers; collect real usage profiles (owner: Priya) — due 2024-11-15
- Finance (Ethan): run 12-month P&L with proposed discount bands and report impact on gross margin (owner: Ethan) — due 2024-11-22
- Sales Ops (Maya): draft AE cheat sheet and produce 2 negotiation play examples (owner: Maya) — due 2024-11-08

Appendix: quick numeric example (6-month smoothing)
- Current commit: 10,000 GPU-hours/month at $2.10/hr list price -> monthly billed revenue = $21,000
- Proposed 6-month taper: month commits = [100%, 90%, 85%, 80%, 80%, 80%] -> avg commit = 87.5%
- If actual usage averages 78% of original commit, idle hours before backfill = (avg_commit - actual_usage) * base -> compute backfill recovered hours at 45% -> net idle reduced.
- Blended effective discount required to keep billed_revenue roughly within 85-95% of full-renewal computed in pricing.tab.

Notes and quick links
- See linked artifacts for simulation code and prior experiments. Add JIRA tickets for instrumenting billing flags.

-- end of working note --
